subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw expose this lease-bound external-orchestrator contract as seven Agentic OS-specific core Gateway methods, or should core provide only a generic extension seam while the Agentic OS protocol remains plugin-owned?
rationale: The PR adds a new persistent, security-sensitive public control-plane contract rather than repairing an established behavior. Repository policy favors owner-plugin behavior and generic core seams, but the contributor asserts that the effective child-session authorization requires core participation.

options.title: Generic core seam plus plugin-owned contract
options.body: Keep only reusable lease/spawn primitives in core and move Agentic OS RPC names, metadata, discovery, and downstream policy into the integration owner.

options.title: Approve a core public contract
options.body: Accept the named Gateway methods in core, but document the permanent API, compatibility policy, security model, and upgrade expectations before merge.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not add a new orchestration contract until a maintainer-sponsored product design establishes the supported external-runtime model.

recommendation.title: Generic core seam plus plugin-owned contract
recommendation.body: Keep only reusable lease/spawn primitives in core and move Agentic OS RPC names, metadata, discovery, and downstream policy into the integration owner.

likelyOwner.reason: A current Gateway or agent-runtime owner must decide whether this becomes a permanent core API; the supplied evidence does not safely identify that individual.
